lessonRef.title: Independent application A: auto personal and mortgage loan concepts
lessonRef.focus: auto personal and mortgage loan concepts

objective: Learners compare invented loan types at the same rate across very different principals and convert annual interest into a monthly burden.
scenario: Hesper is an invented eighth grader modelling two pretend loans at 6% a year: an invented $180,000.00 mortgage concept and an invented $24,000.00 auto loan. All figures are invented for the exercise.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute one simulated year of interest on Hesper's invented $180,000.00 mortgage concept at 6%.

prompts.text: How much interest accrues in the first year?

tasks.directions: Convert that annual interest into a monthly figure, then compute the auto loan's annual interest at the same rate.

prompts.text: What is the monthly interest on the mortgage concept?
How much interest does the auto loan accrue in a year?

tasks.directions: Convert the auto loan interest to a monthly figure and compare the two monthly burdens for Hesper.

prompts.text: What is the monthly interest on the auto loan?
How much larger is the mortgage concept's monthly interest?

tasks.directions: Both loans carried the same rate.

prompts.text: Explain why the same 6% produces such different burdens in Hesper's two loans, and what else besides rate a borrower should compare.

remediation: If a learner compares rates directly, convert both of Hesper's loans into annual dollar interest before any comparison is drawn.
extension: Ask the learner what auto-loan rate would produce the same monthly interest as Hesper's mortgage concept, and what that shows.
